newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Contal lowers 1996 sales volume estimate.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Contal lowers 1996 sales volume estimate.

text.p: Grupo Continental, a bottler of Coca-Cola, said Friday it had reduced its estimate of sales volume growth in 1996 to a range of 1.5 to 2.0 percent, down from five percent previously.

"We started the year estimating growth of five percent (in sales volume) compared to 1995, but we have adjusted it and now expect to finish the year with an increase of 1.5 percent to two percent," Miguel Angel Diaz, deputy director of finance for the company, told Reuters.
Sales volume should reach 197.5 million unit cases in 1996, up from 194.525 million in 1995, he said.
Grupo Continental, also known as Contal, is based in Tampico, Tamaulipas, in northern Mexico. It bottles Coca-Cola products for seven Mexican states.

Diaz attributed the downward revision of the sales volume estimate to a price increase and the lagging recovery of the economy for ordinary Mexicans. He said he did not expect any more price increases this year.
Diaz also said Contal on Friday launched its new Chispa soft drink in Durango and Zacatecas states.
